scenario_stem:
Harbourview Hotels Group operates 4 coastal resort hotels in Country X with 210 staff, including 36 reception and housekeeping supervisors. Revenue last year was $9.6m. Guest complaints about room cleanliness rose from 42 to 78 per year after 2 experienced housekeepers left, and staffing is running 12% below budget. The human resources manager wants to dismiss 3 supervisors whose teams receive the most complaints, claiming this will lift standards quickly. Other directors argue the supervisors deserve support and training instead, because recruitment to replace them would be costly and disruptive.

The board must decide between dismissing the 3 supervisors on performance grounds or keeping them while funding a 6-week retraining programme costing $18,000. Dismissal carries a risk of unfair dismissal claims if correct procedures are not followed, while retraining diverts cash needed alongside a $240,000 refurbishment loan. The manager presents both options at Friday's board meeting and must recommend one.

scenario_stem:
Kestrel Steel Components is a private limited company employing 340 workers at its Country X factory producing pressed steel brackets. A major customer cancelled a $1.9m annual contract, cutting the order book by 30%. The owners consider downsizing by making 60 workers redundant to cut costs. Average redundancy pay would be $12,000 per worker. The factory has 18 workers under 2 years of service and 27 with over 15 years of experience. Directors also debate a 12-month 4-day-week trial instead, saving $1.1m a year in wages with no job losses.

The board must choose between 60 compulsory redundancies now or the 4-day week trial, which holds the 340 jobs but cuts every worker's take-home pay by 20%. Redundancies would reduce annual wage costs by $1.5m but strip out experienced skills; shorter hours protect skills but may push good workers to full-time jobs elsewhere. The managing director decides next month.

scenario_stem:
Clearline Contact Centre, an independent call-answering agency in Country X, employs 150 full-time agents paid the legal minimum of $8.00 per hour on 38-hour weeks. The government will raise the legal minimum wage to $9.00 per hour from January, adding $296,400 to the agency's annual wage bill (150 agents x $1.00 x 38 hours x 52 weeks). Clearline operates on a 5% profit margin and handles 9,000 calls per month. Its largest client, a utilities firm, contributes $480,000 of work a year and refuses to accept a price rise.

The board is weighing two responses: pay the higher legal minimum wage and absorb the cost, or cut 12 agents (about 8% of staff) and raise call charges by 6% to recover the extra expense. Agent morale is already low after pay froze for 2 years, and call quality scores fell from 91% to 84%. A decision is expected within 3 weeks.

Benefit 2: Legal compliance [k]; paying at least $9.00 from January avoids fines and tribunal action [app], protecting the 5% profit margin from penalties and bad publicity that could frighten the utilities client [an].

scenario_stem:
Ironhold Construction is a civil engineering contractor in Country X employing 85 operational staff, of whom 11 are women (12.9%). It is bidding for a $14m hospital refurbishment and needs a new site supervisor. Two candidates applied: Priya, an internal engineer with 6 years at Ironhold, and an external male candidate with 4 years as an assistant supervisor elsewhere. Some directors favour the external candidate, arguing clients 'trust a familiar type'; other directors say this is discrimination against Priya on gender grounds.

The board must appoint the supervisor before the tender is submitted in 5 weeks. Promoting Priya is cheaper and quicker, with no agency fees; hiring the external candidate costs $9,500 in fees and 8 weeks of notice. Ironhold has already signed a contract promising equal opportunity recruitment, and a discrimination claim could mean compensation and damage the hospital bid.

A new high-speed packing line was installed in March, and 3 workers have suffered hand injuries since it started. A health and safety inspection found missing guards and weak training records, and the business was fined $28,000. The board is recruiting 24 temporary workers and induction training takes 2 weeks. The operations director wants off-the-job training at a college costing $12,000, while the production manager prefers cheaper on-the-job coaching by line leaders.

The board must choose the training method before the 24 temporaries start in 4 weeks. Off-the-job training gives structured expert instruction away from the noisy line but removes staff from production; on-the-job coaching is immediate and free but risks passing on bad habits. The next inspection is in 10 weeks and must find clear improvements.

scenario_stem:
Copper Kettle Cafe Company runs 8 cafe outlets across Country X with 92 staff, mostly part-time, earning $2.4m a year. Each outlet holds a 15-minute verbal briefing before every shift covering daily specials and hygiene reminders, at 7:00 and 16:30. The operations manager wants to scrap briefings and use printed notes in the staffroom instead, arguing that kitchen noise, missing staff and latecomers drown out key messages; 40% of staff missed at least one briefing last month. Shift leaders argue verbal briefings let staff ask questions and feel involved.

The head office will pilot one method for 8 weeks. Verbal briefings cost nothing but depend on quiet, attendance and attention; printed notes cost $600 a month but reach absent staff. Wrong-order complaints rose to 26 last quarter and one allergen incident cost $3,500 in refunds.

scenario_stem:
Northgate Freight Services is a haulage firm in Country X operating 6 depots and a fleet of 140 trucks with 260 drivers. Head office issued a 46-page written handbook last year covering new fuel-saving and roadside safety rules, plus weekly emails. After one driver missed a loading note and $30,000 of refrigerated goods were rejected, the board debated how to communicate the revised rules: keep the written handbook and emails, or hold 30-minute depot briefings between shifts at $25 per driver per briefing. The handbook cost $18,000 to print and translate.

The board must decide how all 260 drivers receive the revised rules from June. Written methods give a permanent record and reach every driver regardless of shift, but may never be read; verbal briefings give instant feedback but clash with night runs. Insurers want evidence that every driver was informed of the safety changes.

Limitation 2: Risk of being ignored [k]; a 46-page handbook translated into several languages is unlikely to be read in full [app], so key rules should be summarised on one page with a signature or reply email to confirm receipt [an].

The intranet's $1,500 monthly cost is modest once set up, but only if most staff actually use it [an], while verbal huddles cost nothing yet cannot prove receipt [an]. On balance, Cardinal should install the intranet but keep noticeboards and huddles for the 252 excluded staff [eval], because replacing noticeboards outright ignores the 18% without access and the outage risk shown in practice [eval].

scenario_stem:
Brightstack Software is a private limited company in Country X that grew from 40 to 85 developers and support staff in 3 years, with revenue of $3.2m. Staff turnover hit 22% and 3 product launches slipped last year. The founders communicate by one-way email memos, and staff say they never hear why decisions are made. The operations director proposes monthly all-staff meetings plus an anonymous suggestion box and quarterly pulse surveys costing $9,000 a year. Two founders prefer keeping email-only memos to protect coding time.

The board decides this month. Meetings consume 1 hour of 85 staff time monthly, costed at $4,400 per session but building feedback, surfacing training needs and improving morale. Email memos are quick and free but give no response channel and may be ignored. The business must decide before 20 new hires start in July.

questions.question_text: Define 'two-way communication'.
questions.model_answer: Two-way communication is communication in which the receiver can respond and give feedback to the sender [2].

knowledge_max_2: receiver can respond / feedback to sender
contrasts with one-way communication

questions.question_text: Explain two benefits of two-way communication for Brightstack Software.
questions.model_answer: Benefit 1: Feedback highlights problems early [k]; pulse surveys would have surfaced the training needs behind the 3 slipped product launches [app]. Benefit 2: Staff feel valued [k]; giving 85 developers a voice could help reverse the 22% staff turnover [app].

knowledge_max_2: feedback highlights problems / training needs
staff feel valued / higher motivation and retention

questions.question_text: Explain two barriers to two-way communication at Brightstack Software and how each could be overcome.
questions.model_answer: Barrier 1: Fear of the founders [k]; junior developers may not challenge two founders who favour email memos [app], so anonymous suggestion boxes and surveys let staff speak safely, surfacing problems early [an]. Barrier 2: Time pressure [k]; 85 busy developers lose 1 hour per monthly meeting, $4,400 per session [app], so keeping sessions short, focused and followed by written summaries protects coding time while still inviting feedback [an].

knowledge_max_2: hierarchy / fear of seniors silences staff
time cost / meeting overload
application_max_2: two founders favour email memos / anonymous suggestion box
analysis_max_2: anonymous channels let staff speak safely
short focused sessions plus written summary protect coding time

questions.question_text: Do you think Brightstack Software should introduce monthly two-way meetings and surveys rather than keep one-way email memos? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: Two-way communication fixes the root problem [k]; with 22% turnover and 3 slipped launches, anonymous feedback would surface training needs and rebuild trust before 20 new hires arrive in July [app]. However, monthly meetings cost $4,400 per session plus $9,000 a year for surveys [k], and two founders argue email preserves coding time across a team grown from 40 to 85 in 3 years [app]. Meetings with a written summary give every voice a route into decisions [an], while memos remain free and fast but leave staff unheard and jumping ship [an]. On balance, Brightstack should introduce the meetings and surveys [eval], because reversing 22% turnover and protecting the July intake outweighs a $4,400 monthly time cost, with memos kept for routine updates only [eval].

meetings cost staff time / memos are free and fast
application_max_2: 22% turnover / 3 slipped launches / 20 new hires / July
analysis_max_2: written summaries give every voice a route into decisions

evaluation_max_2: overall recommendation: adopt meetings and surveys
